findings.highlight: all that’s left is to treat them just for show
findings.evidenceJa: 形だけの処置を施すだけだった
findings.governingReading: Only precautionary or formal treatment remained once the wounds had largely closed.
findings.explanation: Just for show implies a sham performance rather than treatment retained as a precaution despite near-complete healing.

findings.highlight: you sure do have a strange body
findings.evidenceJa: ほんとデタラメな体ね
findings.governingReading: Your body is truly absurd or impossible.
findings.explanation: Strange weakens Rin’s forceful judgment that Shirou’s recovery violates ordinary bodily sense.

findings.highlight: come after my neck one day with an axe
findings.evidenceJa: 手斧を持って俺の首を狙ってくる
findings.governingReading: come after his neck one day carrying a hand axe
findings.explanation: The English removes the compact hand axe from Shirou’s mock-archaic execution image.

findings.highlight: it’s still too far beyond human
findings.evidenceJa: 不死身すぎる
findings.governingReading: it is far too close to invulnerability
findings.explanation: The English makes the complaint vaguely superhuman rather than about the apparent inability to kill Shirou.

findings.highlight: my healing power is not as strong as [r]Shir
findings.evidenceJa: 私の自然治癒はシロウほど強くはありま
findings.governingReading: my natural healing is not as strong as Shirou’s—
findings.explanation: A raw control token leaks into the displayed line and breaks Saber’s interrupted realization.

findings.highlight: Saber looks away.
findings.evidenceJa: セイバーは視線を下げた
findings.governingReading: Saber lowers her gaze.
findings.explanation: The English changes downward withdrawal into an unspecified sideways aversion.

findings.highlight: Saber’s spirit has been low
findings.evidenceJa: いつもの覇気が薄れている
findings.governingReading: Her usual commanding vigor has faded.
findings.explanation: Low spirits recasts diminished force and presence as ordinary sadness or depression.

findings.highlight: something she doesn’t want to talk about
findings.evidenceJa: それが言いにくい事である
findings.governingReading: something difficult for her to say
findings.explanation: The English turns visible difficulty voicing the answer into a definite desire not to discuss it.

findings.highlight: character
findings.evidenceJa: 英雄としての気質
findings.governingReading: his disposition as a hero
findings.explanation: Character drops the specifically heroic quality Saber uses alongside ability to distinguish the two Archers.

findings.highlight: the basic limit
findings.evidenceJa: 一度に呼び出せる限度数
findings.governingReading: the maximum number that can be summoned at one time
findings.explanation: The English removes simultaneity, which is the premise allowing a survivor from the previous war to be an eighth present Servant.

findings.highlight: He’s someone you couldn’t beat even when you were properly summoned?
findings.evidenceJa: 士郎とは違う、きちんと召喚されて敵なしだった貴女
findings.governingReading: Unlike your present contract with Shirou, even when properly summoned and without equal, you could not beat him.
findings.explanation: The English omits both Rin’s comparison to Saber’s current handicap under Shirou and her claim that Saber had been unmatched.

findings.highlight: Saber certainly is invincible.
findings.evidenceJa: セイバーとて敵無しというワケじゃない
findings.governingReading: Even Saber is not without opponents as a swordsman.
findings.explanation: mirror moon states the direct opposite, declaring Saber invincible immediately before the source names Berserker as a superior close-combat opponent.

findings.highlight: a Servant that remains from the previous war
findings.evidenceJa: 前回からそのまま残ったサーヴァント
findings.governingReading: a Servant who has remained continuously since the previous war
findings.explanation: The English weakens the emphatic continuity that makes Rin’s survivor hypothesis distinct from a new eighth summon.

findings.highlight: what she said matches what I’ve been hoping for since yesterday
findings.evidenceJa: 俺が昨日から思い描いていた希望のカタチだった
findings.governingReading: Her theory itself takes the concrete shape of the hope he has imagined since yesterday.
findings.explanation: Matches reduces the narration’s image of an abstract hope suddenly acquiring a possible form.

findings.highlight: Herpe
findings.evidenceJa: ハルペー
findings.governingReading: Harpe.
findings.explanation: The Noble Phantasm name is misspelled as the unrelated English-looking “Herpe.”

findings.highlight: a Buddha thing
findings.evidenceJa: お不動さんのアレ
findings.governingReading: that object associated with Fudō or Acala
findings.explanation: The English replaces Rin’s recognizable colloquial deity reference with a vague and inaccurate “Buddha thing.”

findings.highlight: most forms of demonic sword are from Northern Europe
findings.evidenceJa: たいていの魔剣の原型って北欧
findings.governingReading: Most prototypes or archetypes of demonic swords are said to be Norse.
findings.explanation: Forms removes Rin’s tentative claim about historical prototypes and substitutes a vague visual category.

findings.highlight: There’s no point in leaving her like that.
findings.evidenceJa: 百害あって一利なし
findings.governingReading: Leaving her alone promises a hundred harms and not one benefit.
findings.explanation: No point flattens Shirou’s comic certainty that unchecked Rin will actively cause harm, chiefly to him.

findings.highlight: I saw Dainsleif, Herpe, Durandal
findings.evidenceJa: 形状だけで言うなら
findings.governingReading: Judging only from their shapes, he identifies Dainsleif, Harpe, Durandal, and the others.
findings.explanation: I saw changes a cautious shape-based identification into direct recognition.

findings.highlight: She glares at me in irritation.
findings.evidenceJa: 悔しそうにこっちを睨む
findings.governingReading: The sentence describing Rin glaring in frustration is commented out.
findings.explanation: mirror moon restores deleted reaction staging.

findings.highlight: I’m hurt if she makes a face like that.
findings.evidenceJa: 困るというか、申し訳ないというか
findings.governingReading: Her expression leaves Shirou unsure whether to feel awkward or apologetic.
findings.explanation: The English invents wounded feelings and removes his mixed embarrassment and guilt.

findings.highlight: hiding a tree in a forest
findings.evidenceJa: 木の葉を隠すなら森の葉の中
findings.governingReading: hiding a leaf among the leaves of a forest
findings.explanation: The English changes the repeated leaf image into a tree and weakens the analogy to one Noble Phantasm hidden among many.

findings.highlight: I just think you’re useless.
findings.evidenceJa: 戦力外だと思ってるだけよ
findings.governingReading: Rin merely regards him as outside the useful combat or analytical strength here.
findings.explanation: Useless broadens a situational jab into a categorical insult.

findings.highlight: I give up honestly.
findings.evidenceJa: 素直にばんざいをする
findings.governingReading: He obediently raises both hands in a literal surrender gesture.
findings.explanation: The English preserves surrender only as an abstraction and removes the comic physical action.

findings.highlight: No, forgetting that, why did I think that?
findings.evidenceJa: いや、そもそもなんでそんな事を思ったのか
findings.governingReading: No—more fundamentally, why did he think that at all?
findings.explanation: Forgetting that reverses the introspective pivot into a request to disregard the issue.

findings.highlight: were perfect
findings.evidenceJa: 完璧なカタチを持っていた
findings.governingReading: possessed perfect form
findings.explanation: The English drops the form or structure that grounds Shirou’s judgment of genuine weapons.

findings.highlight: I deflected it with my sword.
findings.evidenceJa: 剣と共に斬って捨てました
findings.governingReading: She cut the proposal down and discarded it along with her sword stroke.
findings.explanation: Deflected weakens Saber’s emphatic and contemptuous rejection into a temporary parry.

findings.highlight: Saber answers honestly.
findings.evidenceJa: 真面目に答えている
findings.governingReading: Saber answers the teasing question in complete earnest.
findings.explanation: Honestly changes the comic contrast from solemn engagement to truthfulness.

findings.highlight: Her eyes seem to be laughing not only at Saber, but at me as well.
findings.evidenceJa: セイバーだけじゃなく、黙ってる俺まで肴にしている
findings.governingReading: Rin appears to be using both Saber and silent Shirou as material for her amusement.
findings.explanation: The English turns the pair’s objectification as teasing fodder into the vague image of eyes laughing at them.

findings.highlight: she drinks the bitter tea and stands up
findings.evidenceJa: 渋めのお茶を一気飲みして立ち上がった
findings.governingReading: She downs the deliberately bitter tea in one gulp and rises.
findings.explanation: The English removes Rin’s unbothered one-gulp response to Shirou’s petty retaliation.

findings.highlight: leaves in a good mood
findings.evidenceJa: 上機嫌の体で
findings.governingReading: Rin leaves wearing an air of good humor.
findings.explanation: The English converts Shirou’s observation of her manner into direct access to her emotional state.

findings.highlight: move her to a room
findings.evidenceJa: 和室に移して
findings.governingReading: move Illya to the Japanese-style room
findings.explanation: The English removes the specific room destination from Shirou’s caretaking plan.

findings.highlight: what I want to tell her is all in a mess
findings.evidenceJa: セイバーにするべき話はまったく出来ていない
findings.governingReading: He has not managed any of the conversation he needs to have with Saber.
findings.explanation: The English invents disorganization in Shirou’s thoughts instead of stating that the necessary conversation has not occurred.

findings.highlight: She tries to block my question
findings.evidenceJa: 俺の言い分を牽制する
findings.governingReading: Her quiet voice checks or preempts the argument he is about to make.
findings.explanation: The English turns Saber’s guarded response to Shirou’s known position into an attempt to prevent a question.

findings.highlight: don’t change the past, but change who you are now
findings.evidenceJa: 昔じゃなくて今から取り戻す方法を取れ
findings.governingReading: Instead of returning to the past, choose a way to reclaim what was lost starting now.
findings.explanation: The English replaces Shirou’s demand that Saber recover a life in the present with a demand to change her identity.

findings.highlight: my body steady with my hands as it’s about to fall
findings.evidenceJa: 後ろに倒れそうになる体
findings.governingReading: his body, about to topple backward, is braced with his hands
findings.explanation: The English omits the backward collapse caused by hearing Kiritsugu named.

findings.highlight: I won to the end
findings.evidenceJa: 私と切嗣は最後まで勝ち残り
findings.governingReading: Kiritsugu and Saber both survived through to the final stage.
findings.explanation: The English removes Kiritsugu from the joint survival that placed the Grail in his hands.

findings.highlight: my father was a Master
findings.evidenceJa: 切嗣が、前のマスターだった
findings.governingReading: Kiritsugu was Saber’s previous Master.
findings.explanation: The English removes both the previous-war relation and the fact that he was specifically Saber’s Master.

findings.highlight: The same hero will not be summoned as a Servant again.
findings.evidenceJa: 同じ英霊がサーヴァントとして召喚される事もない
findings.governingReading: The same Heroic Spirit is not ordinarily summoned again as a Servant.
findings.explanation: Hero replaces the Fate-specific posthumous category and blurs the rule Saber says she uniquely violates.

findings.highlight: I do not think I need to tell you when he spoke to me.
findings.evidenceJa: それがなんであるかは、言うまでもない
findings.governingReading: She need not say what those three utterances were.
findings.explanation: The English changes the implied content of Kiritsugu’s three Command Spell orders into their timing.

findings.highlight: he did not have anything that you would call emotion
findings.evidenceJa: 彼には情というものが存在しなかった
findings.governingReading: He possessed no human affection, attachment, or mercy.
findings.explanation: The English makes Kiritsugu literally emotionless, contrary to Saber’s narrower distinction between cruelty and a lack of 情.

findings.highlight: he treated himself only as an object
findings.evidenceJa: 彼本人もまた、自身を道具としてしか見ていなかった
findings.governingReading: He too regarded himself as nothing more than a tool.
findings.explanation: Object weakens the exact parallel: Kiritsugu instrumentalized himself in the same way he instrumentalized Saber.

findings.highlight: my memory is my only truth
findings.evidenceJa: 俺にとってはそれだけが真実だ
findings.governingReading: For Shirou, the childlike man who adopted him is the truth that matters.
findings.explanation: The English shifts the claim from the person Shirou knew to the reliability and exclusivity of his own memory.

findings.highlight: summoned me in a legitimate way
findings.evidenceJa: 正規の手順で私を呼び寄せました
findings.governingReading: summoned her through the regular formal procedure
findings.explanation: Legitimate adds moral or legal approval where Saber contrasts ordinary ritual preparation with Shirou’s anomalous summons.

findings.highlight: Servants would not exist
findings.evidenceJa: サーヴァントは現れない
findings.governingReading: Servants would not appear or be summoned there.
findings.explanation: The English turns a condition of manifestation at a Grail site into a claim that Servants cannot exist at all without a present Grail.
